author: agent:claude-code
message: Recording the known exception to rust.features-additive.

title: BigFloat's default precision: per thread with std, one global without (a known exception to features-additive)
body: The baseline's rust.features-additive (advice) says a feature never changes a behaviour another crate may rely on. The std feature changes one: BigFloat::set_default_precision sets the calling thread's precision with std (thread_local) and the whole program's without (an AtomicU32, since core has no thread-locals), so a build where some crate turns std on changes what a no_std user of set_default_precision sees. Kept as a known exception (the user's call, 2026-10-08): the no_std path is in practice embedded and wasm targets, mostly single-threaded, where one global default is fine, and a per-thread default can't exist there. Everything else std adds is API (streams, Source::stream) or performance (runtime AVX2 detection, cached FFT plans and BigFloat constants), with the same results. The docs of default_precision / set_default_precision say both behaviours.
